title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 4
preview: Ten managers, zero mercy. 112 points rotting on a bench, a commish who can't pick his own QB, and an 0-6 team hoarding draft picks like canned food. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Wow, that just happened. What's next? Weeks 1–3 are in the books, Week 4 is here, and nobody is safe, least of all the commissioner.
facts_note: Every fact is real Sleeper data: Weeks 1–3 results and lineups, transactions, injuries, and Week 4 matchups. "Projected" = Sleeper Week 4 projections in league scoring for lineups as set Thursday Oct 1 around 5 PM ET (lineups can change). A roast among friends.

entries.roast: THE Dictator. Commissioner, rule-maker, self-appointed king, and somehow the only man in America who can't figure out which of his own quarterbacks to start. Week 1 he started Bo Nix for 1.75 fucking points, benched Jordan Love's 21.85, and lost to a rookie GM who'd been in the league for about fifteen minutes. Week 3 he benched Bo Nix and Bo Nix dropped 25.5. You're losing coin flips to the coin, Ryan, and you wrote the rules for the coin. He traded for Dylan Sampson and cut him before he played a single snap, the most expensive way anyone has ever said "never mind." Then he ran Michael Mayer, Terrance Ferguson and Juwan Johnson through his tight end spot like a divorced guy on a dating app. And the worst part? He still leads the league with 500.5 points. Dumb as hell and rewarded for it. That's not a commissioner, that's a nepo baby who hired himself.
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman (0-6). Projected 151.5 to 131.0, with Chase, Olave, Bowers, and two QBs he's going to fuck up the order of anyway.
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 20 and posts about it in the group chat like he personally liberated France.

entries.roast: Brad has Josh Allen AND Patrick Mahomes and he's 3-3. You own the two best quarterbacks on Earth and you're .500. That's a Michelin-star chef working the fryer at a Golden Corral. He's eaten a league-worst 560.5 points against, and in Week 1 his 153.1 got steamrolled by Taylor's 232.5, the biggest score of the year. That's not bad luck, that's the fantasy gods keying your car. Week 3 he started Jadarian Price for 0.2 points. ZERO POINT FUCKING TWO. Meanwhile Kenyon Sadiq dropped 26.0 on his bench. And this week Price is questionable and STILL starting over Kamara. The team's called The Implication, and the implication is that Brad will keep starting Jadarian Price until one of them files a restraining order.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo. Projected 142.3 to 118.3. Price (8.1, questionable) starts over Kamara (10.0) AGAIN, and Breece Hall is doubtful.
entries.prediction: Brad wins, because even Jadarian Price can't lose to Cardillo's RB room. Probably.

entries.roast: FIVE AND ONE with ZERO waiver moves. The man won't touch the waiver wire like it's a public toilet seat. His Sleeper name is RyansHero. A grown-ass adult named himself after the commissioner like he got him at Build-A-Bear. He started Colston Loveland for a big fat 0.0 in Week 1 and won anyway, because he played Drew. Malik Nabers gave him 1.1 in Week 2 and he won anyway, because Taylor shit the bed with 88. Second-softest schedule in the league (358.3 against). You're not a contender, you're a guy getting dealt pocket aces by a dealer with cataracts. And he traded DK Metcalf for Malik Willis. Jacob looked at a Pro Bowl wide receiver and said "nah, I'd rather have a clipboard."
entries.this_week: vs Nick Kasik. Projected 151.9 to 155.8, a 4-point underdog. Jahmyr Gibbs (24.9 projected) has to carry this fraud again.
entries.prediction: Projections lean Kasik, but if Gibbs goes nuclear Jacob goes 7-1 and still doesn't make a single fucking waiver claim.

entries.roast: Brian benched Bryce Young's 36.05 in Week 1 and still won, which tells you how pathetic everyone else is. He's left 94.9 points on his bench, second-most in the league. That's ordering a ribeye and eating the parsley. He paid a 2027 2nd for Terry McLaurin, and McLaurin gave him 3.4 points in Week 1. That's paying for a lap dance and getting a firm handshake. Now Caleb Williams is doubtful, so Mr. SukmyDitkasbro is starting Deshaun Watson off waivers at superflex. In 2026. When your Plan B was last relevant during Covid, your season is held together with duct tape and denial. His only loss was to Ryan by 7.4, and Ryan will bring it up at every draft until 2040.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado. Projected 147.7 to 140.0, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22.4 projected) coming off 45.0 and 37.5.
entries.prediction: JSN bails his ass out again, Brian goes 7-1, and leaves another 30 on the bench because he's allergic to setting a lineup.

entries.roast: Nick put up 85.55 in Week 2, the lowest score of the season, and lost to Nick Cardillo, the ONLY team Cardillo has beaten all year. Losing to Cardillo is getting dunked on by a guy in Crocs. He started Quentin Johnston for 2.4 while Jake Ferguson put 20.3 on the bench. In Week 1 David Montgomery scored 29.9 on the bench. So this week Nick benched Montgomery AGAIN for Aaron Jones. Montgomery isn't your RB, he's the friend you only call when you need a ride, and he keeps showing up with touchdowns like a psycho. The team's called BaldBy22, and the only thing thinner than that hairline is Nick's grasp of his own depth chart.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox. Projected 155.8 to 151.9, the highest set-lineup projection in the league this week. Bijan (22.1) is the engine.
entries.prediction: Nick wins a close one and Montgomery scores 20 on the bench, just to piss him off.

entries.roast: The rookie GM is 5-1, Win-Now No. 1, beat the commissioner in his first game ever, and STILL hasn't set a team name. He's playing as his username like a guy who shows up to a wedding in his work polo. He has the oldest roster in the league (29.2 value-weighted). Derrick Henry is 32, Christian McCaffrey is 30. That's not a backfield, that's a fucking Life Alert commercial. He's acquired T.J. Hockenson three separate times. That's not a roster move, Mike, that's a toxic ex, and Hockenson knows you'll always take him back. Week 2 he started DJ Moore for -0.1 and benched Travis Kelce's 27.1. NEGATIVE points. Moore would've helped more by staying in the parking lot.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano. Projected 150.2 to 152.3. He's starting a questionable DeVonta Smith over Mike Evans, and Jalen Hurts (16.9) over Kyler Murray (18.1) at superflex.
entries.prediction: Two points either way. Henry stiff-arms Father Time one more week, and Mike drops Hockenson a fourth time to celebrate.

entries.roast: Kyle has left 112.45 points on his bench, the most in the league. His bench could make the fucking playoffs. Week 1 he benched D'Andre Swift's 34.4. Week 3 he benched Sam Darnold's 33.45. In Week 2 he scored 182.1, the second-best score of the week, and lost to Brad by four. He's eaten 535.55 points against, second-most in the league. The team is named after Gronk, a man who retired TWICE, and at least Gronk knew when to quit. Kyle started Cameron Dicker for 2.0 and then 1.0 in back-to-back weeks. That's not a kicker, that's a cry for help with a tee.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet. Projected 152.3 to 150.2, the tightest matchup of the week. Now he's starting Darnold (16.4) over Stafford (16.9), chasing last week's points like a drunk chasing the ice cream truck.
entries.prediction: Kyle wins by less than what he leaves on his bench. Book it.

entries.roast: Taylor dropped 232.5 in Week 1, the best score of the season, then shit out 88.2 in Week 2. That's going from the Super Bowl to a Super 8 motel in seven days. He paid Fernando Mendoza AND a 2027 2nd for Jaxson Dart. Dart gave him 1.0 point as a starter and is now on IR, so his superflex is Marcus Mariota, a sentence that should come with a wellness check. He's cycled through six defenses since August. Six. He's been through more NFL defenses than a fucking practice squad. Kyle Pitts gave him 1.5 in Week 3. The team's named EastLansingNatureBoy, the first time Michigan State and "nature" have been in a sentence that didn't end with a couch on fire.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill. Projected 140.0 to 147.7. Brock Purdy (20.3 projected) is the only adult in the room.
entries.prediction: Taylor loses by 8 and grabs a seventh defense out of pure spite.

entries.roast: Drew is 0-6. His all-play record is 4-23, so in 27 tries he's out-scored somebody exactly four times. He made four trades in Week 1. Four. He made more deals than a cartel and has less to show for it. He traded for Rashid Shaheed, started him for 1.4 points, and cut him a week later for Kirk Cousins. Then 38-year-old Kirk Cousins was his best player in Week 3. Your MVP is a guy with a senior discount. He benched Cam Ward's 21.35 in Week 2, then this week dropped Cam Ward for Geno Smith. He's hoarding eight draft picks, including three 2027 2nds, because Drew's entire strategy is "next year," which is what every guy says at the bottom of a bottle of Fireball.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer. Projected 131.0 to 151.5. TreVeyon Henderson (9.4) is starting at flex while Isaiah Likely (11.5) sits. Of course he is.
entries.prediction: 0-8. Drew loses to the commish AND the median, then trades for three more 2nds before the Sunday night game ends.

entries.roast: Coastal Elites. Elite at absolutely fucking nothing. Travis Etienne is out, Jonathon Brooks is on IR, Zach Charbonnet is on PUP. This RB room isn't a depth chart, it's an urgent care waiting room. His Houston defense scored -3.65 in Week 1. NEGATIVE. They'd have helped more by staying home. Brandon Aubrey, the best kicker alive, gave him 1.0 that same week. He's scored the fewest points in the league (322.5), and his one win came against Kasik's 85.55, the worst score of the season. That's bragging that you beat a toddler at Mario Kart while the toddler was napping. He picked up AJ Dillon, then dropped him for Jaylen Wright, who's projected for 4.0 this week. In a STARTING spot.
entries.this_week: vs Bradley Kochheiser. Projected 118.3 to 142.3, the lowest projection in the league. Two QBs (Lawrence 20.5, Maye 18.4) and a rosary.
entries.prediction: 1-7. Coastal Elites gets bent over and goes back to the waiver wire like it's the Cheesecake Factory menu.
